newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan sailor unrepentant over Gandhi attack.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan sailor unrepentant over Gandhi attack.

text.p: A Sri Lankan sailor who struck then Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi with a rifle butt at a guard-of-honour ceremony in Colombo 10 years ago has said he never regretted his gesture of defiance.

Wijitha Rohana Wijayamuni was quoted by the independent Sunday Times newspaper as saying he hit Gandhi because he opposed an accord between the neighbours that he feared could lead to the division of the country.
Gandhi visited Sri Lanka in July 1987 to sign the Indo-Lanka peace accord, which sought to devolve power to minority Tamils and sent Indian troops to disarm Tamil separatist rebels.

The accord was opposed by sections of the majority Sinhalese community who feared it could be a stepping stone to the separate state Tamil rebels are fighting for in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
There were widespread riots in protest against the accord.
"I saw the peace accord as something that would destroy our country," Wijayamuni, a Sinhalese, told the Sunday Times.

"When the entire nation was against it, the leaders went ahead with it," he added. "I felt I had to do something to disrupt it. When I decided to hit the prime minister, I knew I could be killed but I was prepared to make that sacrifice."
Wijayamuni's blow landed on Gandhi's shoulders and neck, without causing serious injury.
Wijayamuni was given a four-year prison term but was released in 1990 under a presidential pardon.
Indian troops sent to Sri Lanka by Gandhi to disarm Tamil Tiger rebels under the accord, ended up fighting them.
They withdrew in 1990 after an inconclusive campaign against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels.
Gandhi was blown up by a female Tamil suicide bomber in 1991 in what is believed to be a revenge killing for his decision to send Indian troops to disarm the Tigers in 1987.
